🇲🇽🚔 CDMX CRIME KEEPS FALLING — 8% DOWN VS 2025, COMPOUNDING GAINS

Mexico City's crime reduction isn't a one-time drop: high-impact offenses fell another 8% in January-May 2026 compared to the same period last year. Homicides specifically dropped 8.8% year-over-year — down to 374 from 401.

The comparison matters because 2025 was already a historically low year for CDMX. Brugada's security strategy is delivering compounding reductions, not a single recovery. All 16 alcaldías continue showing decreases, with over 10,000 detained and 41 criminal cells dismantled in just five months.

🔥🇲🇽 SEMARNAT DROPS CHARGES AGAINST GRUPO MÉXICO — BUT THE 2.2 BILLION PESO BILL STAYS

Mexico's environment ministry withdrew its criminal complaint against Grupo México for the 2014 Río Sonora disaster — the worst mining spill in the country's history. 40,000 cubic meters of acid copper sulfate dumped into the river. 22,000+ residents poisoned across 8 municipalities.

The catch: it's conditional. Grupo México must deliver a 2.2 billion peso settlement — 16 water treatment plants, a regional hospital expansion in Ures with a heavy metals lab, and real-time water monitoring. If they fail, criminal charges come back. By February 2026, one-third had been paid.

The 2023 complaint named three subsidiaries for negligence, environmental crimes, and corruption. Semarnat didn't forgive — it leveraged.

🇲🇽🏥 3.87 BILLION PESOS — NEW IMSS HOSPITAL RISES ON MEXICO'S NORTHERN BORDER

Sheinbaum and Sonora Governor Durazo inspected the new IMSS Hospital General de Zona in San Luis Río Colorado — now 44% complete. Built by military engineers on 35,000 square meters: 120 beds, 24 specialties, 5 operating rooms, intensive care, hemodialysis, chemotherapy, and rehabilitation services.

The 3.87 billion peso facility serves 128,000+ derechohabientes in one of Mexico's most remote border cities, replacing a subzone hospital that couldn't meet the region's needs. First phase delivery: early 2027.

Sonora alone is getting six new hospitals with over 40 billion pesos in healthcare investment. Durazo: "Health is a right for all Sonorans."

🚨🇲🇽 EX-FEDERAL POLICE CHIEF ARRESTED FOR FORCED DISAPPEARANCE

Mexico's FGR arrested Raúl Campos Espinosa — former chief of the Sixth Gendarmería Regiment of the now-extinct Federal Police — for the forced disappearance of a victim in September 2017. He was captured in La Piedad, Michoacán on June 20.

A federal judge ordered preventive detention and set a three-month supplementary investigation period. The Specialized Office for Human Rights presented evidence that Campos Espinosa "as a federal public servant, probably participated in the disappearance of a victim."

The old Federal Police was dissolved in 2019 after decades of infiltration by organized crime. The uniforms are gone — but the cases aren't.

🇲🇽🛢️ Sheinbaum lays out Mexico's energy doctrine in three lines. "Energy production in Mexico must have at least three characteristics: First, guarantee national sovereignty. Second, reduce environmental impacts — sustainability. And third, social justice." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexicali, Baja California A physicist with a PhD in Energy Engineering who once worked inside CFE. Sovereignty comes first.

🇲🇽⚡ "When López Obrador arrived, CFE generated 30% of Mexico's electricity. When he left, 54%. We will leave it at 60%." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, inaugurating the Mexicali combined-cycle plant Mexico's public power utility is steadily reclaiming the share neoliberal reforms tried to hand to private generators. Today's new 653 MW plant in Mexicali adds capacity under public control.
